messages:
maya: Anyone know where the KV/prefix cache dashboards live? Noticed a drop in prefetch hit-rate ~08:45 UTC, alerts started firing. Need quick pointers to graphs + lightweight triage steps before I dig in.

ops-bot: ALERT: KV_PREFETCH_HITRATE_DROP firing on cluster-prod (group: kv-prefetch, severity: page)

liam: Grafana folder: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/kv-prefetch/prefix-cache-overview
liam: Key panels to check: "prefetch_hitrate_1m", "prefetch_hitrate_5m", "prefetch_evictions" and the "prefetch_request_volume" heatmap.
liam: Quick PromQL to reproduce the ratio:```
sum(rate(kv_prefetch_hit_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_prefetch_request_total[5m]))
```
liam: If traffic is bursty switch to [15m] or use increase() for coarse checks.

sanjay: For logs use Loki:```
{app="kv-service"} |= "evicted key" | json | line_format "%{prefix} %{reason}"
```
sanjay: Also check for OOM or GC churn in host logs around 08:30-08:50. Eviction spikes usually mean either memory pressure or a recent config/deploy.

nora: Current alert is absolute: trigger when hit-rate < 0.7 for 5m. That's noisy for low-volume prefixes. I'd recommend changing to a relative drop compared to baseline or adding a minimum request volume.

maya: I muted the alert group briefly while we triage. Can someone propose the alert change?

alex: I can open a PR. Proposal: require >200 reqs in the 5m window and use a 10m for the `for:` value. Example snippet:```yaml
- alert: KVPrefetchHitRateDrop
  expr: (sum(rate(kv_prefetch_hit_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_prefetch_request_total[5m]))) < 0.75 and sum(increase(kv_prefetch_request_total[5m])) > 200
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "KV prefetch hit-rate low ({{ $labels.cluster }})"
    runbook: "https://wiki.redwood.example/kv-prefetch-triage"
```

sanjay: Add a note in the PR about denominator pathology: small denom -> noisy fraction. Also add a Grafana link to the alert description so oncall can jump.

liam: I rolled a canary at 08:28 that touched the prefetch config (reduced in-memory buffer). Might have induced evictions around 08:30-08:35. I'll pull the rollout logs and check pod eviction metrics.

nora: If PR changes are approved, let's include a short blameless entry in the incident doc: what happened, mitigation, alert change, owner.

devex-bot: Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.example/kv-prefetch-triage — contains triage checklist, PromQL, Loki snippets, and rollback guidance.

alex: Opening PR now, will include: Grafana panel links, Loki queries, the PromQL used above, and a note about minimum volume. CC @sanjay @nora for review.

maya: Thanks — I'll attach deploy timestamps and the incident snippet once we confirm root cause. If liam confirms the canary caused evictions we can revert or tweak buffer size. :thumbsup:
